title: Backdrop Filter outputs only preffixed version

regression.commit: 2694a18 Handle properties with auto fallback implementation

impact: 21 reactions, 17 comments; duplicates #785, #1229 (closed), #1086, #1327 (open). Hit via Panda CSS, Tailwind, rspack, Next.js/Turbopack, and Vite 8, which now defaults build.cssMinify to lightningcss. The pattern `backdrop-filter: X; -webkit-backdrop-filter: X` is common in hand-written CSS. Firefox and Chromium don't support -webkit-backdrop-filter, so the effect silently disappears there.
summary: When a rule has `backdrop-filter` followed by `-webkit-backdrop-filter`, FallbackHandler dedupes the second into the first slot and overwrites it with the second declaration's prefix (WebKit only), so the unprefixed declaration is lost. This happens with any targets, including none. `filter` / `-webkit-filter` has the same bug, which is harmless in current engines because both alias -webkit-filter. Prefixes should be merged when the values are equal, and both declarations kept when the values differ.
repro: 695-repro.mjs (+ -chrome-only, -notargets, -order, -filter, -filter-prop, -diffval variants). Input `.a { backdrop-filter: blur(10px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px); }`, minify, targets chrome 120 + safari 15 -> `.a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)}`. Reversed order -> `.a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px);backdrop-filter:blur(10px)}` (correct). Different values (`blur(10px)` then `-webkit-` `blur(4px)`) -> `.a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(4px)}`.
evidence: repro.mjs: wrong on local master, 1.33.0 and every release from 1.21.0 on; correct (with a duplicate) up to 1.20.0. Bisect: 1.20.0 -> 1.21.0. git log v1.20.0..v1.21.0 on prefix_handler.rs gives 2694a18, which added the `dest[index] = ...` replacement that ignores the prefix. Chromium 153 probe: CSS.supports('-webkit-backdrop-filter','blur(1px)') = false, so the output has no effect. equivalence.mjs with the CLI output (chrome 120, safari 15): NOT EQUIVALENT, backdrop-filter blur(10px) -> none. user-select and mask-image with the same ordering are fine (PrefixHandler and mask handler merge prefixes correctly).

fix.approach: In FallbackHandler, for prefixed properties (Filter, BackdropFilter): when the new value equals the stored one, OR the prefixes and re-resolve them via targets.prefixes, as PrefixHandler does. When the values differ and the prefixes differ, push a new declaration instead of overwriting. Open PR #1259 does essentially this and has tests for equal and differing values. Open PR #1284 merges prefixes even when the values differ, which loses the first value, and hand-edits the generated src/prefixes.rs, so it shouldn't be merged as-is.

draftReply:
Thanks for the patience on this one. It's confirmed and still happens on 1.33.0. When `backdrop-filter` comes before `-webkit-backdrop-filter` in the same rule, the minifier merges the two and keeps only the prefixed one. Chrome, Edge and Firefox don't support the prefixed form, so the blur disappears there. It started in 1.21.0. For example, `.a{backdrop-filter:blur(10px);-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)}` becomes `.a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)}`, with or without targets. `filter`/`-webkit-filter` take the same code path.

Workaround until a fix lands: put `-webkit-backdrop-filter` before `backdrop-filter`. That order is kept correctly, and Lightning CSS adds or removes the prefix based on your targets anyway. #1259 proposes a fix. #785, #1086, #1229 and #1327 are the same issue.
notVerified: Safari wasn't checked in a browser (only Chromium is available). Whether Safari 18+ still needs the prefix (PR #1284's claim) is a compat-data question for scripts/build-prefixes.js and wasn't checked. PRs #1259 and #1284 weren't built or tested.
